$comment: Herdr large-DB refresh budget (parent WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W). The `default` profile is measured by the default-suite ratchet test (packages/herdr/src/large-db-refresh-budget.test.ts); the `full` profile (~2,600 items / ~124 MB, the operator-observed scale) is run on demand with `npm run test:perf:large`. A metric exceeding its recorded baseline plus documented headroom fails the ratchet — re-baseline deliberately with `npm run test:perf:large -- --json --update-budget`.

commands.fullScaleDist: npm run build && npm run test:perf:large -- --json --target dist
commands.rebaseline: npm run test:perf:large -- --json --update-budget  (add --target src|dist to pick the invocation)

acTargets.note: Parent epic acceptance criteria at ~2,600 items / ~100 MB (WL-0MVJC1EQX001QR9W): a default-view refresh ≤ ~1.5 s p95 wall, ≤ ~200 ms aggregate event-loop blocking, a documented per-spawn peak-RSS budget below the ~130–145 MB/spawn pre-change baseline and ≤ ~300 MB aggregate for a single pane, write → reflect ≤ ~2 s p95, one consolidated `wl worklist` read per refresh and zero spawns when idle. `enforced` flips true once a full-scale baseline within target is recorded (F7 re-verification).

regression.note: CPU time (process.resourceUsage for the harness plus the per-spawn CPU from the WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE instrumentation) is the load-independent regression gate, with 100 % headroom because the tsx `src` target varies ~50 % run-to-run on a shared host. Wall time and event-loop blocking get 200 % + a 500 ms / 100 ms floor; peak and aggregate RSS keep a tighter 25 % headroom so memory regressions still fail promptly.

dist.method: /usr/bin/node dist/cli.js <argv> — built CLI, warm runs after a priming refresh; CPU/RSS from the WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE spawn records

src.method: /usr/bin/node node_modules/.bin/tsx src/cli.ts <argv> — tsx target, warm runs after a priming refresh; CPU/RSS from the WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE spawn records
